points.description: States that a C++ program begins executing at the main function (main(), the main() function, or the function named main). Wording such as 'execution starts at main', 'the program's entry point is main', or 'control goes first to main()' earns full marks. Answers that name some other function or say execution starts at the first line/statement of the file do not earn the marks.
points.partial_credit: Half to three-quarter credit when main is mentioned but the idea that execution begins there is missing or unclear.

levels.says: Mentions main (e.g. 'in the main part of the program', 'the main body') but does not say that this is where execution begins.
Identifies main as the starting point but hedges or muddles it, e.g. says execution starts at main only 'usually', or mixes it with starting at the first line of the program.

rubric.notes: Full marks for saying a C++ program starts executing at the main function (main()), in any wording. Part marks when main is named but the answer does not clearly say execution begins there. No marks for answers naming another function or saying execution starts at the first line of the source file.
